learning_outcomes.text: Students can phenomenologically describe the structure of fixed-wing aircraft and the fundamentals of their aerodynamics, and calculate the flow processes on airfoil profiles and the forces that occur.

Students can describe the fundamentals of aviation measurement technology and electronic flight control, as well as the structure and function of aviation actuators and sensors, partly calculate them or analyze them systemically, and thus assess the applicability of the named topics in automatic flight control.

syllabus_topics: Stall and Measures to Improve Stall Characteristics
Functional Principles and Basic Structure of Cockpit Systems
Aircraft Sensors (Aerodynamic, Inertial, Laser, Radar, and Satellite-Based)
Design and manufacturing of measuring devices or actuators in practical exercises

assessment_methods.method: Exam for MABB441A (written or oral or presentation)
Exam for MABB442A (written or oral or presentation)

assessment_rules: The examination performance is taken in two individual examinations. The weighting is equal for both events according to ECTS points. For MABB441A, a graded written exam (60 min) or graded oral exam (20 min) or graded presentation (20 min) is required. For MABB442A, a graded written exam (60 min) or graded oral exam (20 min) or graded presentation (20 min) is required. Participation and involvement in the exercises, as well as the successful completion of assignments, are prerequisites for admission to the exam. The module grade for MABB440A results from the grades of MABB441A and MABB442A with equal weighting.
bibliography: C.C. Rossow, K. Wolf, P. Horst, Handbuch der Luftfahrzeugtechnik, Hanser 2014
Bernard Etkin, Dynamics of Atmospheric Flight
Stephen Corda; Introduction to Aerospace Engineering
